items.headline: Stocks plunge Friday: S&P 500 down 3.7%, Nasdaq down 5.3%, worst week in 18+ months
items.note: The S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39 (down 8.6% for the week) and entered a correction, more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record. The Dow fell 1.9% to 48,147.33 and the Nasdaq fell 5.3% to 22,617.73, now negative for 2026. AI and chip stocks led the drop.

items.headline: Chip stocks crater: Nvidia down 13.8%, semiconductor index down 10.7%
items.note: Micron, AMD and Broadcom each fell 12% to 14%. Investors doubt that AI companies' high valuations and heavy spending can be justified. Nvidia is down more than 25% since the Huang leadership scandal began.

items.headline: Anthropic falls 9.1% to $88.30, still above its $83 IPO price
items.note: The stock is about 23% below the $115.10 peak it hit a day earlier. Its first week as a public company coincided with the AI sell-off.

items.headline: Election results favoring slower data center buildout add to AI worries
items.note: AP listed this as one factor in Friday's sell-off. Less data center construction would mean less demand for chips and cloud capacity, which affects the AI industry you want to work in.

items.headline: Nvidia: Bessent's 10-day deadline for the board lands around Nov. 25
items.note: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Treasury Secretary Bessent wants an outside successor and answers on whether shell companies funneled Nvidia chips to China. I found no board response yet.

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield falls to 4.93% as investors flee stocks
items.note: The yield dropped from 5.04% as money moved into government bonds. Brent crude rose 0.6% to $92.57 amid tensions tied to the U.S. war with Iran. Michigan consumer sentiment rose from last month.

items.headline: Fed meets Dec. 8–9; a quarter-point hike was about 77% priced in after the October jobs report
items.note: October payrolls rose 165,000 and unemployment fell to 4.1%. That odds figure dates from early November and may have changed after this week's sell-off. The November jobs report is due Dec. 4.

items.headline: Tech layoffs pass 142,000 this year, but data science demand has held up better
items.note: Layoffs.fyi counted over 142,000 tech layoffs as of Nov. 11. Indeed data cited by one outlet says data and analytics demand has held up better than tech overall, though entry-level hiring is mixed. An AI-driven slowdown could make internships more competitive, so apply early.

items.headline: NYC startups raised $270M+ across 11 deals the week of Nov. 8–14
items.note: AlleyWatch's weekly roundup highlights AI company Hatz AI's $24M round. Local funding was still flowing before this week's sell-off, which could slow later rounds.

learn.explain: When investors get scared, they often sell risky assets like stocks and buy ones seen as safe, such as US government bonds. Heavy buying pushes a bond's price up, and because price and yield move in opposite directions, the yield falls. On Friday the 10-year Treasury yield dropped to 4.93% from 5.04% while stocks plunged. That pattern is called a flight to safety. It doesn't always happen, but it is a common sign of fear in the market.
